contracts.web: src/core/pulsarPanHold.ts: press = one immediate tick, then a 100 ms browser interval of pulsarPanTick using the stored step; a press while held keeps the single running timer. WEB lifecycle: stops on primary pointer up, pointer cancel, capture loss, window blur, page hidden, inactive host, committed load, modal open (tick refused) and unmount; the click that follows a pointer press does not step again. WEB keyboard adaptation (the native buttons have no OnClick, so they cannot be keyboard-panned): a step runs on the button's native click event when its stored pointerPress suppression flag is clear, and no timer starts; Enter usually clicks on keydown and Space on keyup. Enter keydowns with KeyboardEvent.repeat=true are stopped by the PLR capture policy before the button; the button latches Enter/Space from keydown to the keyup it receives and prevents Enter's click while Enter is latched, also for a keydown with repeat=false; a repeated or latched Space keydown is ignored and Space still clicks on keyup. Latched keys are forgotten on keyup, button blur, window blur, a hidden page, an inactive host, a load and a modal, because their keyup may never reach the button. No one-step-per-physical-press, remote-input or assistive-technology guarantee is claimed; a click steps only when the stored pointerPress suppression flag is clear. A tick whose redraw Number cannot represent is refused ('display-unsupported'), which stops the hold. Browser interval cadence vs Windows WM_TIMER resolution/coalescing is not claimed equal. |window| ≤ 1e12 s. Pointer cancel/lost capture release the hold but leave pointerPress set; the next non-keyboard click can be swallowed. This is a preexisting web limitation, not native pointer or assistive-input parity.

contracts.web: Number, not x87 Extended: an admitted tiny nonzero gain (for example 1e-320) can make the quotient overflow to ±Infinity where Extended stays finite. Such a placement is refused with a visible 'number-unsupported' status; the previous cursor, readout and measurement and the loaded bytes are kept, and a fully refused gesture creates no pending entry;an accepted earlier placement in that gesture stays recordable after a refused MouseUp (WEB Number-domain policy). A later accepted placement replaces the refusal status. No zero substitution, no lower gain limit and no reordered arithmetic is introduced.

contracts.observed: Called after the panel's axis/trace repaint. For each stored time not below Single 0x56c440 (vertical +0xc, reference +0x16; jb skips at 0x56c374/0x56c3b7): x = Round((t − start)·zoom/dt), then 0x56c448 recomputes t from x (re-quantization) and draws only when x ≥ 0. Horizontal value +0x20 not below 0x56c440 (jb 0x56c3fa): y = Round(base[ch] − v·100·gain·factor), then 0x56c6dc without recomputing the value; it draws and stores only for 0 ≤ y < base[ch]. A skipped or rejected cursor is not drawn on the repainted panel, and its stored pixel, value and readout are not rewritten.
contracts.staticData: Single 0x56c440 decodes directly to 0.0 (coordinator static data decode, COORDINATOR-correction-triage/static-data-decode.json). Static evidence only: it does not establish runtime FPU comparison or rounding parity
contracts.web: Each panel cursor carries verticalVisible/referenceVisible/horizontalVisible. A placement sets it (x ≥ 0, or an accepted y), so a negative time or value is drawn right after a manual click. A redraw that skips the entry or rejects its y clears it, keeping the stored pixel, time/value, readout and measurement; a later redraw with a valid projection draws it again. A vertical or reference line is drawn only on a client pixel 0 ≤ x < 400. Keyboard arrows step from a line drawn there; otherwise they use a fixed web edge origin (pixel 0, or row base − 1 for the horizontal cursor). WEB Number boundary: a projection that is not finite in Number (for example v·100 overflowing before gain and factor bring it back, where Extended would not overflow) is not attributed to the native out-of-range rejection. The whole zoom, pan, pan tick or factor change is refused with 'display-unsupported' and changes nothing: no partial re-quantization, no hidden line, the same display, cursors and measurement. The arithmetic order is kept; no gain floor or zero is introduced, and no x87 equivalence is claimed.

contracts.observed: MouseDown: left sets drag flag 0x5dd and places the own cursor by mode 0x57c+ch (0 vertical, 1 horizontal); right sets 0x5dc and places the reference cursor on all three panels. MouseMove acts only with ssLeft (0x08) / ssRight (0x10) while the matching flag is set. MouseUp: clears the flag after the final placement, then 0x57f+ch := IsEmpty || highest < ch; when that is false, Record (+0x464) is enabled.
contracts.web: x,y are clamped to integer client pixels [0,399]×[0,Height[ch]−1]; the native code can receive captured coordinates outside the panel. A WEB toggle maps the primary button/touch to the reference cursor; keyboard arrows act as one click per press. This extra gesture bookkeeping is WEB,not native x87; a y rejected by 0x56c6dc is the native rule and still marks the panel pending
